translations.answer: FDDP can improve convergence from poor warm starts by retaining and contracting shooting-node dynamics defects during early line search, but defect closure does not certify friction, torque, collision, or hardware safety constraints.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: A contact sequence and differentiable rigid-body action models are available.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Hardware inequality constraints are added and independently checked.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Multi-contact gait, jump, and flip optimization.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Quadruped and biped models evaluated in the paper.
translations.confidence_rationale: Convergence curves, diverse maneuvers, and the pinned analytical implementation support the mechanism; confidence is capped because evaluation intentionally omits torque and friction-cone constraints.
translations.evidence.0.note: Shows FDDP defect contraction, convergence, and runtime while documenting omitted inequalities.
translations.evidence.0.title: Crocoddyl: An Efficient and Versatile Framework for Multi-Contact Optimal Control
translations.title: Why does multi-contact trajectory optimization allow dynamics defects during early iterations?
